rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice when someone or something is unlucky or not favored by fortune.

example.english: I didn't win the draw this time either; that's unfortunate.
example.traditional: 我今次抽獎又唔中，真係唔好彩。
example.jyutping: ngo5 gam1 ci3 cau1 zoeng2 jau6 m4 zung3 zan1 hai6 m4 hou2 coi2

rows.note: Use this for an unfortunate event or outcome that brings real misfortune, rather than merely being regrettable.

example.english: The accident caused one person to die; that was unfortunate.
example.traditional: 呢單意外搞到一個人死咗，真係不幸。
example.jyutping: ni1 daan1 ji3 ngoi6 gaau2 dou3 jat1 go3 jan4 sei2 zo2 zan1 hai6 bat1 hang6

rows.note: Use this when unfortunate means regrettable or a pity.

example.english: It's unfortunate that the tickets are sold out, so we'll have to go another time.
example.traditional: 可惜啲張飛已經賣晒，我哋唯有下次先睇。
example.jyutping: ho2 sik1 di1 zoeng1 fei1 ji5 ging1 maai5 saai3 ngo5 dei6 wai4 jau5 haa6 ci3 sin1 tai2

rows.note: Use this when unfortunate means unsuitable, unsatisfactory, or not ideal.

example.english: It's unfortunate that this trial's results are unsatisfactory, so we need to change the plan.
example.traditional: 今次試驗結果唔理想，我哋要改個方案。
example.jyutping: gam1 ci3 si3 jim6 git3 gwo2 m4 lei5 soeng2 ngo5 dei6 jiu3 goi2 go3 fong1 on3
